speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions and tell me when the wrist pain and fever started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall being bitten by a tick during your camping trip, and have you noticed any expanding red rash or flu-like symptoms in the weeks prior? I would also like to examine your wrist for signs of inflammation and request an erythrocyte sedimentation rate test.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists are highly characteristic of secondary syphilis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Secondary Syphilis
